newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks weak at midday, near session lows.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks weak at midday, near session lows.

text.p: Wall Street shares were battered by midday on Friday, trading near session lows after strong economic data drove the bond market down and gave investors an excuse to take profits in stocks.

A double dose of data which came in above forecasts -- the July employment report and the National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) index -- revived lurking inflation fears and sent markets lower, analysts said.
The Dow Jones Industrial average was down 111 points, or 1.36 percent, to around 8111.
The Nasdaq composite slid eight points to 1586 and the long bond, whose lower yields have recently propelled stocks higher, sank 1-26/32 to 6.44 percent.

"We got low unemployment, jobs creation and a strong NAPM figure," Robert Froelich, chief investment strategist at Kemper Funds, said. "The combination of these numbers, even if there was no sign of wage inflation, caused the stock market to think about the risk of higher rates."
Bonds and stocks started their downward spiral after the NAPM reported its index of manufacturing activity read 58.6 in July, up from 55.7 in June.
The closely-watched price component, which is an indicator of manufacturing sector pricing pressures, rose to 53.6 for the month, versus 48.1 in June.
This group said the overall index rose to its highest level in 2-1/2 years, while the production indicator hit the strongest level in more than 9-1/2 years.
"The rise in the prices paid knocked the bond market down and brought some profit-taking into the stock market," Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments, said.
